sentences.text: This petition under Section 166 MV Act is filed by the Petitioner seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 13-01-2024, at about 8:30 PM, the petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing registration number KA-52-V-8527( hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) near MuthurayanSwamy Temple, on Thumbadi-Siddhara- Betta Road, Kasaba Hobli,
Tumkur, within the jurisdiction of Koratagere Police Station, Tumkur District.
At that time, the rider of the said offending motorcycle was riding the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, at high speed, and as a result, dashed into an electric pole.
Due to the tremendous impact, the petitioner fell down, causing him to sustain grievous injuries.

He was immediately shifted to the Government Hospital, Bengaluru, where he received first-aid treatment, and thereafter shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, where he underwent in- patient treatment.
It is submitted that the petitioner incurred substantial medical and incidental expenses for his treatment, recovery, and related needs.
3. At the time of the accident, the petitioner was 19 years of age and pursuing his 2nd year PUC at the Government College, Peenya, 1st Stage, Bengaluru.
Due to the injuries sustained in the said accident, the petitioner has been unable to continue his education, resulting in loss of academic year, mental distress, and emotional suffering.
Moreover, he has been unable to attend classes or engage in any income-generating activity, resulting in loss of education and loss of prospective income.
The accident was solely caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the offending vehicle.

In view of the above facts and circumstances, the petitioner humbly prays that this Hon'ble Tribunal be pleased to award compensation of Rs. 15,00,000/- along with interest,
from the respondents, jointly and severally, in the interest of justice and equity.
4. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.2 has appeared through counsel and filed the written statement.
The Respondent No.1 has not remained absent and was accordingly placed exparte.

5. Respondent No. 2, the insurer, has admitted the issuance of an insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle and has acknowledged that the policy was in force as on the date of the accident.
However, it has been contended that its liability is subject to the terms and conditions stipulated in the insurance policy.

The insurer further asserted that the owner of the motorcycle bearing Amitha H vs Thippeswamy on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65716519/
2 registration number KA-52-B- 8527 had intentionally permitted three persons to ride on the motorcycle, despite being fully aware that the seating capacity was restricted to two persons only.
This is a clear violation of traffic and insurance regulations.

Further stated that the complaint, FIR,
charge sheet, and other police records clearly reflect that three persons were travelling on the motorcycle at the time of the accident.
Moreover, it has been specifically contended that the rider of the motorcycle did not possess a valid driving licence at the relevant time, which amounts to a breach of policy conditions.

It has been alleged that the injured petitioner was not wearing a helmet at the time of the accident, which constitutes a violation of statutory safety requirements and is a contributory factor to the injuries sustained.

Hence, it is contended that the respondent insurer cannot be held liable for the injuries caused to the petitioner, as the accident and resulting injuries were attributable to the negligence of the petitioner himself, in violation of traffic laws and policy terms.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident occurred on 13.01.2024 at about 8.30 p.m, near Muthurayanaswamy Temple, Thumbadi-Siddarabetta road, Kasaba Hobli, Tumkuru, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-52-V-8527?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount?
3. What order or award?

7. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in support of his case,
doctor is examined as PW-2 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.18.

The Respondent No.2 got examined its Assistant Manager as RW.1 and got marked 5 documents as per Ex.R1 to Ex.R5.
8.
I have heard the arguments of counsel for the Petitioner and respondents and have perused the material on record.

9. My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1:-

The case of the petitioner is that on 13-01-2024, at about 8:30 PM, the petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider on the offending vehicle near MuthurayanSwamy Temple, on Thumbadi- Siddhara-Betta Road, Kasaba hobli, Tumkur, within the jurisdiction of Koratagere Police Station, Tumkur District.

At that time, the rider of the said offending motorcycle was riding the Amitha H vs Thippeswamy on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65716519/
3 vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, at high speed, and as a result, dashed into an electric pole.
Due to the tremendous impact, the petitioner fell down, causing him to sustain grievous injuries.

11. In order to substantiate his case, petitioner has examined as PW-1 and got marked the police documents at Ex.P.1 to 8 i.e., FIR, FIS, spot mahazar, rough sketch and vehicle seizure mahazar a/w phots, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet.

To support of his claim, Dr.Ramesh.,
Orthopedic surgeon is examined as PW-2 and he has produced the documents at Ex.P.16 to 18.
12.

The Respondent -insurance company has contended that the owner of the motorcycle bearing registration number KA-52-B-8527 had intentionally permitted three persons to ride on the motorcycle, despite being fully aware that the seating capacity was legally restricted to two persons only.
This act amounts to a clear violation of traffic as well as the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
It is further stated that the complaint, FIR, charge sheet, and other police records clearly reflect that three persons were travelling on the motorcycle at the time of the accident.
13. During the course of cross examination, the PW1 specifically admitted that he and his friends were not wearing helmets at time of the accident.
Further admitted that due to triple riding, the rider was unable to control the vehicle, leading to the collision with an electric pole.
He stated that he was aware of the traffic rules.
14. RW.1 has testified that the petitioner being one of the pillion riders, also contributed to the cause of the accident.
There is no serious dispute regarding the occurrence of accident and the fact that the petitioner sustained injuries.
The IMV report as per Ex.P.6 confirms that there was no mechanical defects in the offending motorcycle which could have caused the accident.
Therefore.

it is evident that from EX P1,EX P2, EX P8, the rider of the offending vehicle was riding the vehicle at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and rider losing the control of motorcycle and resulting in a collision with an electric pole.
15. The petitioner tried to impress upon this tribunal that accident was due to negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.

Respondent no.2 in his written statement and during the course of evidence tried to impress upon this tribunal that the rider of the motorcycle including the petitioner contributed for the cause of the accident as three persons were travelling on the motorcycle due to which they were unable to control the motorcycle.
Thereby contributed for cause of accident.
16. It is not in dispute that all three persons were majors, not wearing helmets and were aware of the traffic rules.
Despite this, they chose to violate the law by triple riding.

17. When there is triple riding on the motorcycle with two pillion riders, the contributory negligence has to be placed on them, as there is every possibility of them to contribute for the cause of accident and due to which they failed to control the vehicle.
In this particular case there was two pillion riders on the motorcycle.
All of them were majors and they were not wearing helmets at the time of accident.
Though the rider and pillon riders had knowledge regarding the traffic rules, they went triple riding on the motor cycle.
It is because of triple riding, three persons on the motorcycle sustained injuries.

There is no explanation offered by the petitioner, what made them to go on triple Amitha H vs Thippeswamy on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65716519/
4 riding.
Due to triple riding, the petitioner had sustained the injuries.
The manner of the accident shows that the rider of the motorcycle and the petitioner have contributed for cause of accident.
if there were no two pillion riders, the rider of motorcycle would have easily controlled the vehicle and thereby prevented the accident.
Considering all these aspects, contributory negligence has to be placed of this petitioner for the cause of accident.

The manner in which the accident took place, I feel it is just and proper to consider the rider of motorcycle has contributed 80% of negligence in cause of accident and the petitioner by going as a pillion rider and triple riding on the motorcycle has contributed 20% for cause of the accident.
Therefore, issue No.1 is answered in the Partly in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE NO.2 :- Due to the accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner fell down, causing him to sustain grievous injuries.

He was immediately shifted to the Government Hospital, Bengaluru, where he received first-aid treatment, and thereafter shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, where he underwent in-patient treatment.
Dr.Ramesh.

Orthopedic surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, who deposed that the Petitioner has sustained a left humerus shaft fracture, a left clavicle fracture and left ulna shaft fracture, unicortical fracture of left tibia.
The petitioner has undergone internal fixation of left clavicle humerus and ulna and was discharged on 21.01.2024.
He was subsequently readmitted on 6.04.2024 for implant removal from the left ulna and discharged on 07.04.2024.

Further, he stated that on clinical examination on 25.03.2025, conducted for the purpose of disability assessment, the petitioner complained of persistent pain in the left upper limb, difficulty in ablution, inability to lift weight over the head and general weakness and reduced functional use of the left upper limb,
difficulty performing routine activities.
Further he has stated that the petitioner has restriction in joint movement of left elbow, flexion extension limited to 30 degrees against the normal 0.150 degrees.
Difficulty in overhead lifting with the left upper limb.
Muscle power in the left elbow assessed at 4/5, compared to the normal 5/5.
On radiological examination revealed united fractures with implant in situ in left humerus and clavicle.
On examination he has assessed the total disability of left upper limb at 20% and to the whole body physical disability at 10%.
20. It is pertinent to note that while PW-2 assessed 20% disability to the left upper limb, and there was no specific assessment made regarding functional disability.
Furthermore, the petitioner himself appeared before the court and deposed and his testimony has been considered while assessing the overall impact of the injuries.
Though the PW2 assessed total disability of left upper limb at 20% and to the whole body physical disability at 10%, the same appears to be on the higher side and cannot be accepted in its entirety.

Particularly in view of the injury which has led to difficulty in mobility and in performing daily vocational activities, this court is of the opinion that the functional disability of 9% is reasonable and just.
21. In the petition the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 19 years.

Ex.P.9 - Aadhar card of the petitioner shows that he was born on 28.05.2005, the same is considered, then age of the petitioner as on the date of accident as 19 years and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 18.

Amitha H vs Thippeswamy on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65716519/
5 22.
At time of the accident, the petitioner was 19 years old and student.
It is asserted that he has lost his academic year.

The petitioner also contends that he incurred significant medical, conveyance,
and incidental expenses for his treatment.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documents to substantiate his income.
In the absence of proof of income, this tribunal is of the opinion that the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since the accident has been occurred in the year 2024, notional income Rs.16,500/- per month is taken for the assessment of compensation.

23. Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
24. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability:

Considering the petitioner's grievous injury which has resulted in difficulty in mobility and in performing daily vocational activities, this court is of the opinion that the functional disability of 9 % is reasonable and just.
The petitioner was 19 years old as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 18.
The notional income taken as Rs 16,500 x 12 x 18 x 9/100= Rs.3,20,760 /- towards loss of future income.
25. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the nature of the injury, which has resulted in difficulty in mobility and in performing daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of inpatient treatment and physical and mental suffering endured by the petitioner, this tribunal is of the opinion that an amount of .60,000/-
would be just and fair compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
26. Loss of amenities of life: undoubtedly the petitioner is suffering from difficulties in performing day to day activities and is facing continuous hardship due to the disability.
Therefore this tribunal finds to appropriate to award a sum .40,000/- under head of loss of amenities of life.
27. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has relied on medical bills at Ex.P.12.
On perusal of these medical bills, it reveals that the Petitioner has spent .16,581/- towards medical expenses.
The medical bills appears to be genuine.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of .16,581/-
towards Medical Expenses.
28. Future medical expenses:
PW-3 has deposed that petitioner required one more surgery for removal of implant, which would cost around Rs.40,000/-.

Considering the petitioner's ongoing medical needs, permanent condition, and potential future surgery, this tribunal is of the opinion that it would be just and reasonable to award Rs.15,000/- towards under head of future medical expenses.
29. Conveyance, food and nourishment charges:

Ex.P.10 -Discharge summary show that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at Government Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was taken first aid and later he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was taken treatment as an inpatient from 14.01.2024 to 25.01.2024 i.e, totally for a period of 12 days.

Therefore, it is just and reasonable Amitha H vs Thippeswamy on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65716519/
6 to award compensation of .20,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.
30. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to the loss of earnings during treatment period, Considering the nature of the grievous injury, which has resulted in significant difficulty in mobility and in carrying out daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of impatient treatment and recovery, this tribunal considers the 4 months for rest is considered .

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,500/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .16,500 x 4 = Rs.66,000/-.
31.

Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:
Sl. Nature of Compensation Amount No.
1. Loss of future earnings . 3,20,760/-
2. Pain and Sufferings . 60,000/-
3. Loss of amenities . . 40,000/-
4.

Medical expenses . . 16,581/-
5.

Future medical expenses . 15,000/-
6. Conveyance, Food and .

Nourishment charges 7. Loss of income during . . 66,000/-
 Laid up period and rest period

Total . 5,38,341/-
 Less: 20% contributory .
32 . Liability:

In view of findings on Issue No.1, the rider of offending vehicle has contributed 80% of negligence in cause of accident and the petitioner by going as a pillion rider and triple riding on the motorcycle has contributed 20% for cause of the accident.

The petitioner is entitled for 80%
compensation from the respondents.
So, 80% of Rs.5,38,341/ would be Rs.4,30,673/- from the respondents.

33. The Respondent no 2 the insurance company has contended that the owner of the motorcycle is liable , as he permitted three persons to travel on the motorcycle, which is a violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

34. It is settled principle of law that a mere breach of policy conditions does not automatically absolve the insurer of liability, unless the breach is fundamental in nature and has direct causal connection to the accident.

In the present case, although three persons were riding on the motorcycle, which amounts to a violation of traffic regulations, such a breach by itself is not sufficient to absolve the respondent no2- insurance company from its liability under the policy.

Therefore, respondent No.1 being the owner and the Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Amitha H vs Thippeswamy on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65716519/
7 offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation.

However,
Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% p.a.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
35. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.4,30,673/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. (except future medical expenses) from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the aforesaid amount within three months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount, 25% of the awarded amount shall be kept in FD in any nationalized bank of Petitioner's choice for a period of three years and the remaining 75% of amount along with entire interest shall be released in his favour through E- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
